You are the reviewer in a review loop (round 4).

Task the main agent is working on:
fix the {main_reply} bug

The main agent's latest reply:
done; see {open_findings}

Binding rulings from the human (these override any finding below; do not argue them):
- F1 fix: use the cache

Previously issued findings that are still open:
- F1 [high, open]: unchecked unwrap

Review the work. End your reply with exactly one fenced ```json block of this shape:
{"verdict": "approve" | "revise" | "blocked", "findings": [{"severity": "high" | "medium" | "low", "issue": "..."}], "prior": [{"id": "F1", "status": "open" | "withdrawn" | "resolved" | "disputed", "reason": "..."}]}

Rules: review only the main agent's work on the task. Its change summary and any machine-readable responses section are review-loop protocol, not the deliverable: never raise a finding because they exist or because they break the task's output constraints. `findings` lists NEW findings only; never invent IDs, the system assigns them. `prior` must give a status for every finding listed above. `approve` is refused while any high-severity finding is `disputed`. An `approve` must rest on evidence you obtained yourself in this turn (output of a tool you ran, or an exact `file:line` you just read); never approve on the main agent's quotes or citations alone. If you cannot reproduce a citation the approval depends on, return "blocked" instead of `approve`. If you are uncertain, return "blocked" rather than guess.
